  children={"Create a post"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/api/posts"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



`uploadedAssetUrls` must be paths returned by the
[upload endpoint](/developers/api-reference/upload-files) (`/uploads/...`)
or Immich proxy paths for an album linked to **this** post's group —
arbitrary URLs are rejected. `latitude` and `longitude` must be
provided together.

Pass `groupIds` instead of `groupId` to **cross-post**: with 2 or more
target groups, the server creates one linked copy of the post per
group. For the author it behaves as a single post — editing or
deleting it edits/deletes every copy — but comments, reactions, and
favorites stay scoped to each group's own copy, and other members can
never tell it was cross-posted. Reactions and comments are *shown*
merged, though: a viewer who belongs to several target groups (always
the author) sees every copy's reactions (one per person) and comments
combined on whichever copy they open (`likeCount`, `reactions`,
`myReaction`, `recentReactors`, `commentCount`, the reactions list and
the comment thread). A member of only one target group sees just that
group's. Every target group must be one you
belong to, or the whole request is rejected with no post created.
Photos sourced from a linked media album (Immich/local) are copied
server-side into Famlin's own upload storage at post time so every
target group can see them without gaining access to the source
album; direct uploads are shared as-is.

Pass `circleId` to narrow the audience from the whole group to one
circle within it. Only members of that circle will see the post, its
comments, its reactions and its photos — including by direct media
URL. The circle must belong to the target group and you must be a
member of it; all other cases are a `403` that deliberately doesn't
distinguish "not yours" from "doesn't exist", so circles you can't
see can't be probed. `circleId` cannot be combined with cross-posting
(a circle belongs to exactly one group), which is a `400`.

Every target group's `allowedPostTypes` (see `Group`) must include
the requested `type` — for a cross-post, **all** target groups must
allow it, or the whole request is rejected with no post created.

`type: "POLL"` creates a poll: `content` is the poll's question
(required, non-empty) and `typeData` carries `{ options, closesAt? }`
— 2 to 10 options, each 1-100 characters. The server assigns each
option a stable id; options can't be added, removed, or edited after
creation. `closesAt` is optional and API-only (no composer support
yet) — once it passes, the poll stops accepting votes. Polls may also
carry `uploadedAssetUrls` like any other post.

`type: "TRIP"` creates a living travel journal: `typeData` carries
`{ title, destination?, startDate, endDate?, coverPhotoUrl?, travelerUserIds? }`
— `title` (1-120 chars) and `startDate` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) are required;
`destination` (≤160 chars), `endDate` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, must not be
before `startDate`), `coverPhotoUrl` (an uploaded `/uploads/...`
path), and `travelerUserIds` (up to 20 other members who may also
check in — the author is always an implicit traveler and is
stripped if included) are all optional. Trips cross-post like any
other type, and a cross-posted trip stays **one** journal: check-ins,
closing, and traveler changes apply to every group's copy. Because of
that, every `travelerUserIds` entry must be a current member of
**every** target group. Check-ins, closing the trip, and changing its
travelers all happen after creation via
`POST /api/posts/{postId}/interactions` (see below).

`type: "ALBUM"` creates a collaborative photo album that **any** group
member (not just the author) adds photos to: `typeData` carries
`{ title, coverPhotoUrl? }` — `title` (1-120 chars) is required,
`coverPhotoUrl` (an uploaded `/uploads/...` path) is optional. Photos
are added after creation via
`POST /api/posts/{postId}/interactions` (`key: "addPhotos"`, see
below), and the author can close the album (`key: "close"`) so no
more photos can be added. Albums cross-post like any other type, and a
cross-posted album stays **one** album whose contributions land in
every target group's copy. The album's photos are stored as its
contribution comments, not on `uploadedAssetUrls`.

`type: "GIFT_LIST"` creates a gift list in **one** family (no
cross-posting, no `circleId`): `typeData` carries
`{ title, occasionDate?, participantUserIds?, drawEnabled?, budget?, exclusions? }`
— `title` (1-120 chars) is required; `occasionDate` is `YYYY-MM-DD`;
`participantUserIds` (up to 49) are the other participants, each a
member of the group (you are always one); `budget` is free text (≤40
chars); `exclusions` are pairs of participant ids that may not draw
each other (symmetric). Only participants can see the post anywhere.
Wishlists, participant changes, settings and the draw are managed
through the Gift lists endpoints afterwards.

`type: "EVENT"` creates an event people can RSVP to: `content` is the
event's title (required, non-empty) and `typeData` carries
`{ startsAt, endsAt?, location?, rsvpDeadline? }` — `startsAt` is
required; `startsAt`/`endsAt`/`rsvpDeadline` are ISO 8601 date-times
(an offset is accepted and normalized to UTC), `location` is free text
(1-200 chars). `endsAt` can't be before `startsAt`, and
`rsvpDeadline` can't be after it. Events cross-post like any other
type; RSVPs happen afterwards via
`POST /api/posts/{postId}/interactions` (`key: "rsvp"`, see below).
